en.summary: Italy's news market is led by national newspapers based in Milan, Rome and Turin, a public broadcaster, RAI, and the commercial television group Mediaset. Corriere della Sera, la Repubblica and La Stampa are the main national dailies, and ANSA, a cooperative of publishers, is the main news agency. Television remains the most-used source of news, and the governance of RAI is closely tied to the governing parties, a long-standing subject of debate. Digital outlets and fact-checkers have grown, and investigative journalism focuses on organized crime and corruption, with some journalists living under police protection. Italy also has a large sports press led by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Regional newspapers are important in Naples, Bologna, Venice and Sicily. Most newspapers use metered paywalls.

faq.q: What are the main national news outlets in Italy?
faq.a: The main national outlets in the directory include Corriere della Sera, la Repubblica, La Stampa, ANSA and Il Post. The Top National News column lists them in editorial order.

faq.q: Which Italian news sites are free to read?
faq.a: Free-to-read outlets include ANSA, Rai News, Sky TG24, TGCom24 and Radio Radicale. The paywall model of every outlet is shown next to its name.

faq.q: Which Italian outlets are publicly or state funded?
faq.a: Public-service outlets include Rai News. Ownership is labeled on every outlet in the directory.

faq.q: Where can I find regional news in Italy?
faq.a: Regional coverage in the directory comes from La Stampa (Piedmont), Il Messaggero (Lazio), Il Mattino (Campania), Il Resto del Carlino (Emilia-Romagna) and Il Gazzettino (Veneto). The Regional & Local column lists every regional outlet.

general-news.intro: These are the outlets Italians use to follow national news: national dailies, the ANSA news agency, the public broadcaster and a calm digital explainer. Paywall model and owner are shown for each outlet.

economy.intro: Italian business news is anchored by a business daily owned by the industry federation, with financial newspapers and investor sites covering the Milan stock exchange, banks and public finance.

sports.intro: Italy has three national sports dailies and broadcasters covering Serie A, cycling, Formula 1 and MotoGP. The outlets below are ordered by editorial relevance.

investigative.intro: Investigative journalism in Italy covers organized crime, corruption and political accountability, through a news magazine, an independent daily, a nonprofit newsroom and fact-checkers.

regional.intro: Regional newspapers in Italy cover Naples and Campania, Emilia-Romagna, Veneto, Sicily and Piedmont.
